name: Superb fairywren
note: Tiny, with a tail held straight up. Breeding males turn bright blue; families hop about the ground together and love a shallow edge to bathe in.

name: New Holland honeyeater
note: Black and white, streaked, with yellow wing panels and a white eye. Quick, restless, and never far from grevillea or bottlebrush.

name: Red wattlebird
note: A big, loud honeyeater with small red flaps of skin on its cheeks. Bold at nectar plants and not shy about the water.

name: Little wattlebird
note: Smaller and streakier than its red cousin, with no red wattles. Often heard before it is seen.

name: Rainbow lorikeet
note: Blue head, red chest, green back. Arrives in noisy groups and turns a bath into a splash party.

name: Noisy miner
note: Grey with a yellow patch behind the eye. A native honeyeater, but a bully: miners often chase smaller birds away from water.

name: Australian magpie
note: Black and white, with that warbling carol. Walks up to the bath rather than flying in, and drinks in long, careful sips.

name: Silvereye
note: A small olive-green bird with a bright white ring around each eye. Often in small flocks that bathe one after another.

name: Spotted pardalote
note: One of Australia's smallest birds, covered in white spots. Usually high in the gum trees, so a visit to the bath is a real catch.

name: Eastern spinebill
note: A small honeyeater with a long, fine, curved bill. Hovers at flowers like a hummingbird, then perches to drink.
